title: [Auth] Register donor and recipient accounts
scope: Create public registration for Donor and Recipient accounts with required personal and contact fields, unique email and phone constraints, and Argon2 password hashing. Public registration must never create Staff or Admin accounts.
acceptance: Valid details create one unique Donor or Recipient account.
Duplicate email or phone values and missing or malformed fields return field-level validation errors without saving a partial account.
Passwords are stored only as strong one-way hashes and are never returned or logged.
The registration endpoint is available at POST /api/v1/auth/register and cannot assign privileged roles.
verification: Automate TC-Auth-01 for valid, duplicate, invalid, and privileged-role attempts.
Inspect persisted credentials and sanitized logs to confirm that no plaintext password is present.

title: [Auth] Implement secure login, logout, and role redirects
scope: Authenticate registered users with server-side sessions, secure cookies, CSRF protection, generic failure responses, login throttling, logout, and redirects to the correct role dashboard.
acceptance: Valid credentials start a server-side session and return the correct role dashboard destination.
Unknown users, wrong passwords, and disabled accounts receive the same generic authentication failure.
The session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite, and state-changing requests require CSRF protection.
Logout invalidates the active session, and repeated failed attempts are throttled with a Retry-After response.
verification: Automate TC-Auth-02 across all four roles, invalid credentials, disabled accounts, throttling, and logout.
Verify LOGIN_SUCCESS and LOGIN_FAILED audit events contain no password or session value.

title: [Security] Establish role-based access control
scope: Implement the Donor, Recipient, Staff, and Admin role model, deny-by-default permission classes, and object ownership checks defined by the SAD role-permission matrix.
acceptance: Every protected view declares a server-side permission policy and denies access by default.
Each role can perform only the operations allowed by the approved permission matrix.
Object-level access limits donors and recipients to their own records and returns 404 for foreign records.
Sensitive denied operations produce protected ACCESS_DENIED audit events.
verification: Automate TC-Auth-03 with positive and negative checks for every permission-matrix cell.
Confirm that changing client-side state cannot bypass server-side authorization.

title: [Profiles] View and update permitted profile fields
scope: Provide GET and PATCH /api/v1/users/me with a per-role writable-field whitelist while keeping role, active status, and medically verified fields read-only to ordinary users.
acceptance: Signed-in users can view their own profile and update only fields permitted for their role.
Valid updates persist and are visible on the next read.
Attempts to change role, active status, verified medical data, or another user's profile are denied.
Validation errors identify the affected field and save no partial change.
verification: Automate TC-Profile-01 for each role, writable fields, protected fields, and malformed input.
Verify sensitive profile changes are audited where required by the event catalogue.

title: [Donations] Schedule and cancel donation appointments
scope: Create donation slots with capacity and donor endpoints to list slots, book an available slot under a row lock, view appointment history, and cancel a booked appointment.
acceptance: Booking calls the shared eligibility engine and rejects an ineligible donor without changing capacity.
An eligible donor can book an available slot and see it in appointment history.
Concurrent bookings cannot exceed slot capacity.
A donor can cancel only their own booked appointment through a valid state transition.
Full, missing, ineligible, duplicate, and forbidden cases return the documented error codes.
verification: Automate TC-Don-01 including eligibility integration, capacity-boundary, and concurrent-booking scenarios.
Exercise booking and cancellation through the donor UI with keyboard navigation.

title: [Donations] Record immutable completed donations
scope: Allow Staff to record a completed donation with donor, date, blood group, quantity or component, status, and screening weight while updating the donor's last-donation date in the same transaction.
acceptance: Only Staff can create a completed donation record with all mandatory validated fields.
Recording calls the shared eligibility engine and rejects an ineligible donor without partial changes.
The record is immutable through the API; corrections use compensating records rather than update or delete.
The donor's last-donation date and DONATION_RECORDED audit event commit with the donation.
The donation appears accurately in the donor's own history.
verification: Automate TC-Don-02 for authorization, eligibility integration, valid creation, rollback, immutability, and history visibility.
Confirm a failed transaction leaves no donation, date update, or audit fragment.

title: [Donations] Prevent duplicate active appointments
scope: Enforce duplicate appointment prevention in both the booking service and a partial unique database constraint for active BOOKED appointments.
acceptance: A donor cannot hold two active bookings for the same slot.
Duplicate requests return 409 duplicate_appointment without changing slot capacity.
Concurrent duplicate attempts create at most one active appointment.
A cancelled appointment does not permanently block a valid new booking where the state model allows it.
verification: Automate TC-Don-03 at the service, API, database-constraint, and concurrency levels.

title: [Donations] Implement donor eligibility rules
scope: Implement eligibility as a shared pure domain function using age at least 18, weight at least 50 kg, and the approved minimum donation interval. Booking and recording integrations are owned by BBMS-F-010 and BBMS-F-011.
acceptance: All eligibility rules are evaluated against the supplied appointment or screening date using the configured blood-bank time zone.
Unsupported donation types fail closed.
The result lists every failed rule with readable reasons and includes the next eligible date for interval failures.
Boundary values for age, weight, and interval follow the approved policy exactly.
verification: Automate TC-Don-04 as table-driven pure-function tests including every boundary, unsupported donation types, and multiple simultaneous failures.

title: [Inventory] Create verified blood-unit records
scope: Allow Staff to create one inventory record for each verified unit, link it to its donation, and assign a unique scanner-friendly unit code.
acceptance: Only Staff can create a verified blood unit linked to an existing completed donation.
Each unit receives a unique unit code suitable for barcode or QR keyboard input.
A valid unit appears in inventory with its initial state and a UNIT_CREATED audit record.
Duplicate codes, unverified donations, missing donations, and forbidden roles are rejected without partial records.
verification: Automate TC-Inv-01 for creation, linkage, code uniqueness, scanner input, authorization, and rollback.

title: [Inventory] Validate mandatory blood-unit data
scope: Model and validate blood group, component, collection date, expiry date, quantity, and status with database constraints and fixed enumerations.
acceptance: Every mandatory inventory field is non-null and validated on the server.
Expiry is after collection, quantity is positive, and blood group and component use the documented enumerations.
Invalid values return field-level errors and save nothing.
Database constraints protect the invariants when application validation is bypassed.
verification: Automate TC-Inv-02 across all blood groups and components, date boundaries, quantity boundaries, and direct constraint failures.

title: [Inventory] Make stock transitions transactional and auditable
scope: Implement the blood-unit state machine for reserve, release, issue, expire, discard, and return. Write an append-only inventory ledger and audit entry in the same locked transaction, with stock derived from unit state rather than a mutable counter.
acceptance: Only documented unit-state transitions are accepted; all others return 409 invalid_state_transition.
Every accepted transition writes exactly one append-only inventory transaction and required audit event atomically.
Available stock always equals the number of unexpired AVAILABLE units and cannot be edited directly.
Concurrent operations cannot reserve or issue one unit twice, and rollback leaves unit, ledger, audit, and stock unchanged.
verification: Automate TC-Inv-03 for every valid and invalid transition, rollback, concurrency, and ledger immutability.
Reconcile computed stock against unit and ledger records after the test matrix.

title: [Inventory] Search safe blood availability
scope: Provide staff unit-level inventory search and recipient aggregate availability by blood group and component, with pagination and independent status and expiry filtering.
acceptance: Search returns only matching AVAILABLE units whose expiry date is after today under the approved boundary rule.
Staff can view paginated unit-level results while Recipients receive aggregate counts only.
Donors and Admins are denied inventory availability access as defined by the permission matrix.
Invalid blood groups or components return documented validation errors.
verification: Automate TC-Inv-04 with all groups and components, expired and near-expiry units, role visibility, empty results, and pagination.

title: [Inventory] Run the idempotent daily expiry job
scope: Schedule a daily Celery job at 00:05 local time to expire eligible units in safe batches, record each run, expose an as_of_date test hook and test-only manual trigger, and alert on failed or missing runs.
acceptance: Units at or beyond the approved expiry boundary become EXPIRED and are excluded from availability.
The job is idempotent, cannot overlap for the same run date, and writes ledger and audit records exactly once per unit.
Every run records status, counts, and sanitized error text in job_run.
A partial failure preserves committed batches, reports FAILED, and can be safely rerun.
verification: Automate TC-Inv-05 with manipulated dates, exact boundaries, old expiries, repeated runs, overlap attempts, and mid-run failure.
Verify monitoring detects a FAILED run or no successful run within 26 hours.

title: [Requests] Submit blood requests
scope: Allow a Recipient to submit validated patient and requirement details and receive a unique request number in PENDING state, with audit and notification side effects where specified.
acceptance: A complete authorized submission creates one PENDING request with a unique human-readable request ID and timestamp.
Patient group, component, units, urgency, hospital, required-by time, and contact details are validated.
Only Recipients can submit requests; forbidden roles and malformed requests save nothing.
The submit action creates the required protected audit record without exposing clinical or contact details in application logs.
verification: Automate TC-Req-01 for valid submissions, every required field, invalid enumerations and dates, authorization, uniqueness, and rollback.

title: [Requests] Review and decide blood requests
scope: Allow Staff to approve, reject, or place a PENDING request on hold through the documented state machine, requiring a reason for rejection and hold and recording reviewer, timestamp, audit, and notification atomically.
acceptance: Only Staff can make request decisions from allowed source states.
Reject and hold require a non-empty reason; approval follows the documented validation rules.
The new state, reviewer, review timestamp, audit entry, and requester notification outbox row commit together.
Invalid transitions return 409 and leave the request unchanged.
verification: Automate TC-Req-02 for every valid and invalid transition, reason validation, authorization, side effects, and rollback.

title: [Fulfillment] Reserve and issue blood safely
scope: Reserve and issue compatible available units for an approved request using FEFO with exact-group preference, row-level locks, one active allocation per unit, transactional state changes, and an Idempotency-Key on issue.
acceptance: Reservation uses the shared compatibility engine to select sufficient compatible AVAILABLE and unexpired units using FEFO and exact-group preference.
Issue uses the same engine to recheck state, availability, expiry, and compatibility inside the locked transaction before fulfillment.
Concurrent requests cannot reserve or issue the same unit, and a repeated idempotency key returns the original result without changing stock twice.
Insufficient stock, incompatibility, invalid state, or unavailable units roll back all allocations, states, ledger, audit, and notifications.
verification: Automate TC-Req-03 for FEFO selection, exact-group preference, rollback, concurrency, idempotent retry, and all documented errors.
Run an end-to-end approval, reservation, and issue workflow and reconcile request, unit, allocation, ledger, audit, and stock records.

title: [Requests] Show owned request status and history
scope: Provide paginated request list and detail endpoints and UI so Recipients can see only their own current state and timestamped history while Staff can view operational requests.
acceptance: A Recipient can list and view only requests they own, including current status and recorded timestamps.
Another user's request returns the same 404 response as a missing request to prevent identifier enumeration.
Staff can view all requests as allowed by the role matrix; Donors and Admins are denied.
Results are ordered and paginated consistently.
verification: Automate TC-Req-04 for ownership, foreign IDs, missing IDs, role access, status history, ordering, and pagination.

title: [Safety] Enforce ABO and Rh compatibility
scope: Implement shared component-aware acceptable_donor_groups and is_compatible pure functions for the approved compatibility matrix. Fulfillment integration is owned by BBMS-F-032.
acceptance: The approved compatibility matrix is represented in one lookup-driven domain engine parameterized by component.
Every incompatible pairing is rejected and every compatible pairing is accepted for each approved component rule set.
Invalid blood groups and components fail closed.
The reusable guard produces the documented 422 incompatible_blood_type error.
verification: Automate TC-Req-05 over the full 8 by 8 donor-recipient matrix for each supported component.
Include explicit universal-donor, universal-recipient, Rh-negative, and invalid-input assertions.

title: [Notifications] Deliver request status notifications
scope: Write notification outbox rows in the same transaction as request status changes, dispatch them asynchronously through a provider adapter, expose each user's notifications, and retry and surface failures without blocking clinical workflows.
acceptance: Approved, rejected, held, fulfilled, and other configured status changes create the correct recipient notification exactly once.
Outbox creation commits atomically with the triggering status change.
The worker sends through the selected or mock provider, retries with backoff up to five times, and records sanitized failures.
Users can view only their own notifications, and provider failure never rolls back the clinical action.
verification: Automate TC-Notif-01 with the mock provider for each transition, retry, permanent failure, duplicate dispatch protection, ownership, and rollback.
Verify the pending-count and failure-rate monitoring thresholds.

title: [Inventory] Alert on configurable low stock
scope: Let Admin configure thresholds per blood group and component, evaluate them after stock-lowering transitions and the daily job, alert Staff on downward crossing, and suppress repeats until recovery.
acceptance: Only Admin can view and change valid thresholds, and every change is audited.
A downward threshold crossing creates one low-stock alert for authorized Staff.
Repeated checks below the threshold do not duplicate alerts while alert_active is set.
The alert state clears when stock recovers to or above the threshold, allowing a later crossing to alert again.
verification: Automate TC-Notif-02 for every transition around the threshold, repeated checks, recovery, concurrent transactions, configuration authorization, and audit behavior.

title: [Reports] Generate operational reports
scope: Generate date-filtered, paginated donation, inventory, request, and issued-unit reports for Staff and Admin, with an optional CSV export that follows the same filters and privacy rules.
acceptance: Staff and Admin can generate each documented report for a valid date range and supported filters.
Report totals and rows match authoritative database records and use consistent time-zone boundaries.
Unauthorized roles are denied and report data excludes fields they should not receive.
Large reports are paginated, and any CSV export matches the filtered result.
verification: Automate TC-Report-01 with seeded records, date boundaries, filters, authorization, pagination, totals, and export parity.

title: [Administration] Manage staff accounts and roles
scope: Provide Admin-only APIs and UI to create, disable, and change roles for Staff accounts, with immediate session revocation and protected audit records.
acceptance: Only Admin can create Staff accounts, disable accounts, or change managed roles.
Disabling an account immediately invalidates all of its active sessions.
Role changes take effect server-side without relying on cached client permissions.
USER_CREATED, USER_DISABLED, and ROLE_CHANGED events record actor, target, outcome, and time.
verification: Automate TC-Admin-01 for each operation, forbidden roles, session revocation, permission changes, validation, and audit records.

title: [Audit] Record and search critical actions
scope: Create an append-only audit log and record helper used inside business transactions, covering the SAD event catalogue and providing Admin-only indexed search by actor, action, time, and affected record.
acceptance: Every catalogued login and critical change records actor, role, action, entity, outcome, IP, correlation ID, and UTC time as applicable.
Business changes and their audit entries commit or roll back together.
The application role cannot update or delete audit rows, and ordinary users cannot read them.
Admin can search paginated audit records by actor, action, date range, and affected record.
verification: Automate TC-Audit-01 for the complete event catalogue, transactional rollback, immutability, authorization, filtering, ordering, and pagination.

title: [Performance] Meet the three-second response target
scope: Instrument and tune search and dashboard requests so at least 95 percent complete within three seconds under an agreed normal project load, using indexes, pagination, query optimization, and response compression.
acceptance: The normal-load profile, dataset size, concurrency, environment, and measurement window are documented.
JMeter results show a 95th-percentile response time no greater than three seconds for search and dashboard flows.
List endpoints enforce pagination with a maximum page size of 100.
Metrics expose request latency and alert when the threshold is exceeded for five minutes.
verification: Execute TC-Perf-01 with a reproducible JMeter plan and attach the summary and raw-result location.
Capture query plans for any tuned high-cost query and rerun functional regression tests.

title: [Reliability] Provide health checks and availability controls
scope: Add a non-sensitive /healthz endpoint, process supervision and automatic restart, a one-minute external probe, and availability reporting against the 99.5 percent monthly target excluding documented maintenance.
acceptance: The public health endpoint reports service readiness without exposing configuration or sensitive data.
Application and worker processes restart automatically after a controlled failure.
Three consecutive failed probes and a five-minute 5xx rate above one percent raise alerts.
Availability reports distinguish planned maintenance and demonstrate how the 99.5 percent target is calculated.
verification: Execute TC-Reli-01 with controlled process and dependency failures and record probe, restart, and alert evidence.

title: [Security] Protect stored credentials and logs
scope: Configure Argon2 as the Django password hasher and central log filtering so passwords, tokens, session identifiers, and sensitive clinical or contact details never appear in storage or logs.
acceptance: New and changed passwords use Argon2 with framework-managed salts and are never stored in plaintext.
Authentication and error paths do not log passwords, tokens, cookies, session IDs, clinical data, or contact details.
Password verification works through the framework and no custom reversible credential storage exists.
Security review documents the configured hasher and sanitization coverage.
verification: Run TC-Sec-01 against registration, login success and failure, validation failures, and unexpected errors, then inspect storage and captured logs.

title: [Audit] Retain protected audit records for one year
scope: Index and partition audit records for search, retain them for at least one year, and implement a controlled purge path that cannot remove records before policy permits.
acceptance: Audit timestamps use UTC and search fields for time, actor, action, and record are indexed.
Records younger than one year cannot be removed by the application or purge job.
Only the controlled retention process can purge eligible records and every run is itself recorded.
Representative retained records remain searchable within the operational target.
verification: Execute TC-Audit-02 with controlled record ages, unauthorized mutation attempts, eligible and ineligible purge cases, and search checks.

title: [UX] Deliver responsive and accessible role dashboards
scope: Build responsive Donor, Recipient, Staff, and Admin dashboards and shared form patterns targeting WCAG 2.1 AA, including labels, keyboard operation, visible focus, readable errors, status text and icons, and 44-pixel touch targets.
acceptance: Each role dashboard exposes the actions and information defined in SAD section 4.5 and no unauthorized data.
Every control has a visible label, full keyboard operation, visible focus, and screen-reader error announcements.
Status never relies on color alone, and destructive actions confirm the affected unit or request details.
Tables adapt to narrow screens and interactive touch targets are at least 44 pixels.
verification: Execute TC-UX-01 with keyboard-only, screen-reader, contrast, responsive-layout, readable-error, and role-dashboard checks.
Attach screenshots or recordings for desktop and mobile layouts.

title: [Recovery] Automate backups and verify restoration
scope: Create a daily 02:00 database backup to encrypted offsite storage, document the restore runbook, monitor backup freshness, and prove a 24-hour RPO and four-hour RTO through a restore drill.
acceptance: A full automated backup runs daily and is copied encrypted to storage separate from the database host.
Retention follows the approved policy and no secret is embedded in source control or job logs.
No successful backup within 25 hours raises an alert.
A documented drill restores a representative backup on a spare environment within four hours and verifies record integrity.
verification: Execute TC-DR-01 and attach backup, alert, restore timing, and integrity-check evidence without exposing production data or credentials.

title: [Security] Enforce TLS and secure transport
scope: Configure Nginx and database connections for TLS 1.2 or higher, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, enable HSTS and required security headers, and reject obsolete protocols.
acceptance: All client-server traffic uses TLS 1.2 or higher and plain HTTP redirects to HTTPS.
HSTS and the documented security headers are present on application responses.
Database traffic uses TLS on the private network.
Obsolete protocols and weak transport configurations are rejected.
verification: Run the transport portion of TC-Sec-01 against public endpoints and database configuration and retain a sanitized inspection report.

title: [Security] Harden server-side authorization
scope: Apply centralized permission classes to every protected API view and recheck the actor's role inside sensitive services so no operation depends on client-side visibility or routing.
acceptance: An automated inventory shows every protected endpoint has an explicit permission class.
Sensitive services reject unauthorized direct calls even when view-layer checks are bypassed.
Object ownership is enforced consistently and foreign objects are not disclosed through response differences.
The implemented matrix matches the approved SAD role-permission baseline.
verification: Execute TC-Sec-02 as positive and negative API tests for every role and protected operation, including direct service tests.

title: [Security] Validate input and prevent injection
scope: Define schema validation for every endpoint, use parameterized ORM queries and template auto-escaping, set Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options, and fuzz high-risk login, donor, inventory, and request inputs.
acceptance: Malformed, oversized, unexpected, and type-invalid fields are rejected before business processing.
No application query is built by concatenating user input, and rendered user content is escaped by default.
Required browser security headers are applied consistently.
Injection and malformed-request probes produce no successful SQL, script, template, or command injection.
verification: Execute TC-Sec-03 with automated fuzz and injection cases on login, donor, inventory, and request forms and APIs.
Review code for raw SQL, unsafe rendering, and unbounded inputs.

title: [Security] Audit security-relevant events
scope: Verify and complete protected audit coverage for login failures, session expiry, role changes, access denial, inventory issue actions, request decisions, and the full SAD security-event catalogue.
acceptance: Every required security event is recorded with actor when known, role, action, outcome, time, IP, and correlation ID as applicable.
Events never contain passwords, tokens, session values, or unnecessary clinical or contact details.
Security events are append-only and visible only through authorized Admin search.
More than 20 failed logins per minute from one address triggers the configured alert.
verification: Execute TC-Sec-04 for each event type, sanitized fields, access controls, transaction rollback, and failed-login alerting.

title: [Security] Expire idle and long-running sessions
scope: Implement configurable sliding idle expiry with a 20-minute default and an eight-hour absolute session limit, returning the standard session_expired response and recording expiry events.
acceptance: Inactive sessions become invalid after the configured idle timeout.
Active sessions cannot exceed the configured absolute lifetime.
Expired sessions return 401 session_expired and the UI redirects to login with a readable message.
Timeouts are environment-configurable to seconds for tests and SESSION_EXPIRED is audited without exposing the session value.
verification: Automate TC-Sec-05 for idle expiry, sliding renewal, absolute expiry, concurrent sessions, disabled accounts, and UI handling.

title: [Decision] Approve compatibility rules by blood component
scope: Obtain an approved rule set for RBC or whole blood, plasma, and platelets because the SRS currently states red-cell-style ABO and Rh rules for every component.
acceptance: The approved donor-recipient matrix is documented for every supported component.
The SRS, SAD compatibility table, API behavior, and TC-Req-05 matrix are updated consistently.
The decision identifies who approved the safety rule and its effective date.
verification: Review the resulting matrices for complete coverage of all eight blood groups and supported components.

title: [Decision] Approve donation intervals by donation type
scope: Confirm whether the 56-day minimum applies only to whole blood and define configurable intervals for every donation type included in version 1.0.
acceptance: Each supported donation type has an approved minimum interval or is explicitly excluded from version 1.0.
The eligibility configuration, SRS, SAD, and boundary tests are updated together.
A safe default and change owner are documented.
verification: Review TC-Don-04 boundary cases against every approved interval.

title: [Decision] Confirm the blood-unit expiry boundary
scope: Confirm whether a unit is unavailable at the start of its expiry date or only after that date, including the blood-bank time zone used at the boundary.
acceptance: One unambiguous date and time-zone rule is approved.
Availability search, the expiry job, SRS wording, SAD domain rules, and TC-Inv-05 use the same rule.
Exact-boundary examples are documented.
verification: Review before, exactly-at, and after-boundary test cases.

title: [Decision] Confirm separation of Admin and Staff duties
scope: Confirm whether Admin is excluded from operational actions such as reviewing requests and reserving or issuing units, as assumed by the SAD permission matrix.
acceptance: The allowed Admin and Staff operations are explicitly approved.
The SRS role descriptions, SAD permission matrix, API documentation, and authorization tests agree.
Any exception preserves least privilege and is justified.
verification: Review every Admin and Staff cell in the permission matrix after the decision.

title: [Decision] Confirm one role per account for version 1.0
scope: Confirm that a person acting as both Donor and Recipient uses two accounts in version 1.0, or approve a multi-role model before account and permission implementation is frozen.
acceptance: The version 1.0 role cardinality is approved and documented.
Registration, user model, permission logic, UX, and test data reflect the decision.
Any deferred multi-role enhancement is recorded as future scope.
verification: Review registration and permission test cases for the approved account model.

title: [Decision] Confirm server-side sessions for version 1.0
scope: Confirm server-side cookie sessions rather than JWT for version 1.0 and document the condition under which an external hospital client would require revisiting the decision.
acceptance: The authentication mechanism is approved before the API contract is frozen.
SRS terminology, SAD ADR-004, OpenAPI security scheme, and session tests are consistent.
External hospital API authentication remains explicitly out of scope unless separately approved.
verification: Review login, CSRF, revocation, idle-timeout, and absolute-timeout test coverage.

title: [Decision] Select the notification provider mode
scope: Choose an email or SMS provider for deployed use or explicitly approve the console or mock adapter for the project demonstration, including secret handling and sandbox constraints.
acceptance: The version 1.0 provider mode and delivery channel are approved.
Required configuration, secret storage, sandbox behavior, rate limits, and failure handling are documented.
The mock remains available for deterministic automated tests.
verification: Demonstrate one successful and one failed delivery through the chosen adapter without exposing credentials.

title: [Decision] Set operational defaults and retention
scope: Approve initial stock thresholds, donation-slot capacities, blood-bank time zone, and backup retention values while keeping the documented settings configurable by authorized roles or deployment configuration.
acceptance: Each required default has an approved value, unit, owner, and configuration location.
Unsafe or nonsensical values are rejected by validation.
The SAD, seed data, environment example, operational runbook, and relevant tests use the approved defaults.
verification: Review threshold, capacity, time-zone boundary, retention, and authorization tests.

title: [Project] Configure the GitHub backlog and sprint board
scope: Create a GitHub Project linked to this repository, add all requirement and delivery issues, expose priority, sprint, story points, status, dependencies, and assignee, and provide useful backlog and sprint views.
acceptance: The Project is linked to the repository and contains every published backlog issue.
Backlog, Sprint 1, and Sprint 2 views show status, priority, story points, and ownership when work is claimed.
Every issue belongs to one sprint milestone, has a story-point label, and remains unassigned until a contributor claims it through the agreed workflow.
Blocked work and decision dependencies are visible before implementation starts.
verification: Audit the Project item count against backlog/issues.json and check every required planning field.

title: [CI] Validate every pull request with GitHub Actions
scope: Add GitHub Actions for pull requests and main that install pinned dependencies, run formatting or linting, migrations and system checks, unit and integration tests, and publish clear pass or fail results.
acceptance: Every pull request triggers the agreed validation workflow.
The workflow uses least-privilege permissions, pinned action versions, dependency caching, and no repository secrets for untrusted code.
A failing test blocks a successful workflow result and provides actionable logs.
The contributing guide lists the local commands corresponding to CI once the application scaffold exists.
verification: Open or use a test pull request to capture one passing run and one intentional failing run, then restore the branch to green.

title: [API] Freeze the OpenAPI contract and Postman collection
scope: Publish the /api/v1 OpenAPI contract for every SAD endpoint, standard errors, session and CSRF security, schemas, examples, role restrictions, pagination, and idempotency, then derive and share the Postman collection used by QA.
acceptance: Every endpoint in SAD section 4.3 appears with request and response schemas, status codes, role restrictions, and examples.
The standard error envelope and correlation ID are defined consistently.
The issue and fulfillment endpoint documents the Idempotency-Key requirement.
The checked-in Postman collection is generated or verified against the same contract and contains no secrets.
verification: Validate the OpenAPI document, run contract checks against the application, and import and execute the Postman collection in a clean environment.

title: [QA] Seed complete test data and notification mocks
scope: Create an idempotent seed_test_data command with all four roles, all eight blood groups, each component, expired and near-expiry units, request states, appointment and eligibility boundaries, and deterministic notification mock behavior.
acceptance: One documented command creates the complete synthetic dataset in a clean test environment.
Repeated execution is safe and produces known accounts and record counts without duplication.
No real personal, clinical, provider, or credential data is included.
Tests can assert notification outbox and delivery behavior without contacting an external provider.
verification: Run the command twice on a clean database, verify expected counts and edge cases, then execute representative tests from every module.

title: [QA] Execute the test plan and publish release evidence
scope: Complete manual and automated test cases, scripts, data, execution logs, defect reports, permission and compatibility matrices, UAT, and the final test summary while updating every RTM row from not-run to pass or a linked defect.
acceptance: Every planned test case has a result and reproducible evidence, including the full compatibility and role-permission matrices.
No critical defect remains open and every high-priority functional and security requirement is verified.
Failures link to defect issues and reruns preserve the original and final outcomes.
The final summary reports execution, pass rate, defect density and aging, requirement coverage, risks, and sign-off status.
verification: Audit every SRS RTM requirement against a design ID, test case, result, and evidence link.
Record UAT outcome and release recommendation from the responsible owner.

title: [Sprint 1] Record the working-product demonstration
scope: Record and upload a one-minute demonstration of the Sprint 1 working product, link the exact tested revision, and document any deviation from the approved SRS, SAD, Test Plan, or sprint backlog.
acceptance: The recording is approximately one minute and shows complete working Sprint 1 flows rather than static screens.
The repository contains or links the recording and identifies the demonstrated revision.
Completed issues and test status are summarized using the sprint template.
Every deviation is documented with impact, rationale, approval status, and follow-up issue.
verification: Play the uploaded recording from the repository location and cross-check demonstrated flows against completed Sprint 1 issues.

title: [Sprint 2] Finalize the demonstration, documentation, and freeze
scope: Record and upload the two-minute Sprint 2 working-product demonstration, complete project and operational documentation, reconcile deviations, and freeze development only after release-readiness criteria are met.
acceptance: The approximately two-minute recording demonstrates the integrated product and identifies the tested revision.
Setup, architecture, API, test, operations, restore, and user-facing documentation are complete and internally consistent.
All deviations from the submitted documents are listed with explanation and final disposition.
The freeze records the final revision, open known issues, test summary, and owner approval, with no open critical defects.
verification: Run the release-readiness checklist, play the uploaded recording, validate documentation from a clean setup, and confirm the frozen revision matches the test summary.
